subject: Security notification: unexpected auth activity; retention & SIG evidence questions
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@healthcorp.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@healthcorp.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unusual auth activity observed on HealthCorp-Redwood integration

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Heads up — our monitoring flagged a set of unexpected auth/token exchanges against our HealthCorp <> Redwood integration this morning (approx 07:45 PST). The activity appears to come from three IPs we don't recognize and involves a small number of failed token-exchange attempts followed by two successful calls that accessed non-sensitive metadata endpoints.

We're in the process of containing on our side, but we need Redwood to:
- Confirm whether you observed any concurrent failed/successful auth attempts tied to HealthCorp API keys or service accounts.
- Preserve relevant logs (auth, token issue/validation, and API access logs) for 90 days pending forensics.
- Provide the contact for your on-call forensics lead so we can coordinate a joint timeline.

Also: our security team will need the SIG/CAIQ packet or an excerpt showing audit log retention policies and IRP contact details so we can complete an internal customer notification. If possible, please indicate whether you can provide SHA256 digests of logs vs. full exports — our legal/compliance team prefers hashed artifacts initially.

Attaching our brief log request template (healthcorp-log-request.csv) to make requests easier.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Lead InfoSec Analyst, HealthCorp
security@healthcorp.com

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@healthcorp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 09:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth activity observed on HealthCorp-Redwood integration

Thanks for the alert, Tom — and sorry you're seeing this. We appreciate the CSV; it's helpful.

Quick status from our side:
- We see corresponding failed token validations from the same approximate window (07:40–07:50 PST). There were no successful API calls that accessed customer data — only calls that hit status/metadata endpoints.
- We've escalated to our on-call incident responder and begun preservation steps. We are snapshotting auth logs, token issuance logs, and the reverse-proxy access logs for the tenant and moving them to a restricted forensic bucket. We will retain these artifacts for 90 days as you requested.

Please find a short acknowledgement attached (initial-incident-ack.txt) and a one-page summary of our incident response process (redwood-ir-proc-summary.pdf).

Our primary contact for the investigation is Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com). She will coordinate any log exports and share the minimal artifacts you need. Naomi Feldman from Compliance is on copy for any evidence transfer / contractual steps.

Next steps we propose:
1) Marissa will confirm within the hour what exact time ranges and log sources we can export as hashes vs full events.
2) If HealthCorp needs full exports, we'll provide a secure transfer link after a short data-share agreement (we can use DocuSign if needed).
3) We'll run token rotations for any suspect keys and share a summary of affected keys (no user creds; only service keys).

Let us know if you want a quick call (we can do a 30-min bridge this morning).

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@healthcorp.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth activity observed on HealthCorp-Redwood integration

Tom — looping in details from our forensics triage.

Triage summary (preliminary):
- Observed window: 2027-01-29T07:38:12Z -> 2027-01-29T07:49:03Z
- IPs: 3 external IPs (stored in the forensic bucket); we are collecting full connection metadata but can provide SHA256 digests on request within 30 minutes.
- Actions: preserved auth-server logs (token_issuer.log), gateway access logs (gateway-access-2027-01-29.ndjson), and service audit trails for the tenant ID.
- Containment: rotated any keys with anomalous usage; issued temporary tokens for HealthCorp in coordination with your team.

Log export options:
A) Hashed digests (SHA256) of each log line — quickest and preferred for initial review.
B) Full export (NDJSON) via encrypted S3 presigned URL — requires a short data transfer addendum (we have a DocuSign template ready).

Please confirm which you prefer. If you accept hashed digests for now, we will attach a small sample in the next message and open a secure transfer link for full exports if needed.

We also have a current SIG/CAIQ snapshot that includes our audit log retention policy and IR contact information. Naomi, can you share that packet and a one-paragraph statement on retention policy to HealthCorp?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Incident Response & Forensics, Redwood Inference
From: security@healthcorp.com <security@healthcorp.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 14:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth activity observed on HealthCorp-Redwood integration

Marissa / Grace,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for preserving the artifacts. HealthCorp will accept hashed digests initially (option A). Please send the sample digests and a checklist of the full artifacts available so our legal team can review before we request a full export.

Also — please send the SIG/CAIQ snapshot and the short retention statement. Once our legal team confirms, we will route the DocuSign data transfer addendum (sample link below) and provide an upload destination for a full export if required.

DocuSign link (provisional): https://docusign.com/HealthCorp-IR-Authorization-12345

Appreciate the coordination. We may request a short postmortem and a remediation summary once the investigation completes.

—Tom (on behalf of HealthCorp Security)
